followup_reviews.Research finding: Retain the closure of Khurcha–Nabakevi and Orsantia–Otobaia as an included, scoped two-crossing episode; other ABL crossings remained available. The affected ordinary crossings are specifically named. Alternative routes, shuttle provision and longer travel do not mean complete cessation of movement across the whole administrative boundary. Retain 4–6 March 2017 onset uncertainty: Public Defender, CoE/Civil Georgia and OHCHR accounts differ. The dated 16 November description supports only qualified confirmation through then, at least 255 calendar days, with no established reopening. The security rationale is explicitly attributed to the Abkhaz authorities through inspected quotations. It is not an endorsement of that explanation; administrative convenience is not silently made an extra rationale. The official Public Defender passage was indexed, the CoE and OHCHR texts and Civil Georgia reports were directly read. OHCHR discloses lack of access; quoted ministry accounts share an origin. The now-redirected historical MFA page is not fresh substantive evidence. All current phase/location coordinates remain null. Named ABL posts are checked for identity, but no boundary line or point binding is approved by this audit. The separate challenge aligns the summary start-precision label with the existing 4–6 March day bounds.
